title: Polish codebreakers break Enigma
summary: In December 1932 the Polish Cipher Bureau began breaking German Enigma ciphers; five weeks before the Second World War it handed its methods and equipment to France and Britain.
why: The foundation of the Allied Ultra codebreaking effort.

unsung.contribution: Broke the German Enigma cipher and gave the methods to Britain and France in 1939.
unsung.recognition: The work stayed secret; the Polish break was first revealed publicly only in a 1967 book, years before Ultra became widely known.
